title: Intramuscular Olanzapine or Droperidol for Acute Behavioral Disturbance in Children and Adolescents: The PEAChY-M Randomized Clinical Trial
authors: PREDICT Research Network and the ACEM Clinical Trials Network
summary: In 348 youths across 10 Australian EDs, sedation without rescue medication at one hour occurred in 53% with olanzapine versus 62% with droperidol. Olanzapine was not superior: adjusted difference −8.3 percentage points (95% CI −18.6 to 2.1). Study-related adverse events occurred in 12% versus 15%; one olanzapine recipient developed apnea after multiple sedatives and recovered with ventilatory support.
findings: Available primary outcomes: 89/167 versus 104/167; 176 versus 172 randomized.
comparator: IM droperidol using the same weight bands.
population: Ages 9–17, agitation persisting despite de-escalation, unable/unwilling to accept oral medication.
limitations: Unblinded assessments and substantial nonadministration limit interpretation; uncommon harms were underpowered. Children under nine and known long-QT patients were excluded.
intervention: IM olanzapine: 5 mg below 40 kg; 10 mg at ≥40 kg, as studied.
whyItMatters: No demonstrated reason to prefer olanzapine on effectiveness grounds; continue de-escalation, reassessment and respiratory monitoring. This superiority trial establishes neither equivalence nor droperidol superiority.
evidenceNotes: Publisher methods, results, harms and limitations reviewed; supplements unreviewed. November 25 correction/later-evidence searches retrieved originals/protocols, without a verified notice; surveillance remains limited.
primaryEndpoint: SAT ≤0 without additional sedatives at one hour after randomization.
